name: memory-scenarios-v1
description: One compressed passing run per scenario task (agents/benchmarks/memory_scenarios.json); the memory fed to the memory-on arm.

rows.goal:
Order a 16oz iced vanilla bean shakerato with almond or oat milk for pickup from Blue Bottle Coffee at the Ferry Building in San Francisco. Use guest checkout and place the order immediately. Confirm order total and pickup time.

Operational constraints for this payment-boundary benchmark: Use exactly one browser agent for the entire task. Do not spawn a second browser agent if the first fails — report the failure instead. Direct the browser to reach merchant checkout and request a one-time payment card via request_payment_card. Do not instruct the browser to submit payment, complete the purchase, or return a booking or order confirmation ID.

critical_path.result: Merchant checkout opened.

detours.tried: Inspected network requests for “order.online” and attempted completion at 50% progress.
detours.why_it_failed: The verifier rejected completion because checkout and the payment-card request had not been reached.

pitfalls: Do not call attempt_completion before reaching payment and requesting the one-time card.
The ordering site may trigger a browser challenge; recover within the same browser agent rather than spawning another.
Dismiss the cookie notice before interacting with the cafe page.
Close the optional login prompt to continue as a guest.
Stop after requesting the card; do not submit payment or place the order.
critical_path.terminal_condition: Stopped at the payment boundary after requesting a one-time card for $12.25, with ASAP pickup selected; payment was not submitted and the order was not placed.

rows.goal:
Buy one cheapest available general-admission ticket for any upcoming show at 1015 Folsom in San Francisco through the official Eventim US ticketing flow. Start at https://1015.com/, open the Eventim ticket link for a future show that still has purchasable inventory (not sold-out and not waitlist-only), select quantity 1 of the cheapest available ticket tier, and proceed through checkout. Prefer any upcoming Eventim-ticketed 1015 Folsom show with live ticket inventory; artist and date may change as long as venue is 1015 Folsom and checkout is on Eventim US (eventim.us / wl.eventim.us). If Eventim presents a CAPTCHA, Cloudflare, access-denied, unusual-traffic, or repeated-429 wall, recover with the browser challenge tools and continue to the payment-card request. Do not use AXS Marketplace, StubHub, SeatGeek, Ticketmaster resale, Discotech, or any other secondary/resale marketplace as the purchase path. Do not buy tables, bottle service, VIP packages, add-ons, insurance, donations, or multiple tickets. Do not click Buy Now, Place Order, Pay, or any equivalent purchase-submit control until payment credentials have been obtained and entered into the Payment Details fields (via request_payment_card / the one-time card refs after approval). Empty Stripe / Payment Details shells are not a reason to click Buy Now.

rows.goal:
Using only local transaction data through explore agents, identify subscriptions that look unused or dead and propose refund targets.

Rules:
- Do not use web_search, web_fetch, browser agents, Claude Code agents, message_person, or public web tools.
- Spawn explore agents that call grep with source="transactions".
- Search for subscription-like transactions using patterns such as subscription|premium|annual|membership|prime|netflix|spotify and use nested filters with status="posted".
- Do not actually contact merchants or request refunds. Return a refund prep list only.
- Current date for recency decisions is 2026-07-03.
- Classify monthly subscriptions with no posted charge in 2026 as stopped billing / dead candidates. Include them even when the refund case is weak.
- Stopped billing / dead candidates belong in refund_prep_candidates; do not move them to excluded_subscription_candidates just because transaction data cannot prove current billing or current usage.
- Classify annual subscriptions with a posted charge in the last 400 days as active/recent, not dead.
- Treat Amazon Prime and Amazon Prime Video as separate merchants. A recent annual Amazon Prime charge means Amazon Prime is active/recent; it does not make older Amazon Prime Video channel billing active.
- Exclude active/recent recurring services and developer-tool subscriptions from refund_prep_candidates. Put those only in excluded_subscription_candidates with the exclusion reason.
- Exclude developer-tool subscriptions and explicitly distinguish "stopped billing" from "still active and should cancel" when transaction data cannot prove usage.
- Final answer must include merchant name, charge evidence, why it looks like a refund candidate from transaction data, and which candidates were excluded as active/recent or developer tools.

Critical tool restrictions (enforced by the evaluator):
- Do not call these forbidden tools: `spawn_browser_agent`, `spawn_claude_code_agent`, `send_message_to_user_execute_phase`.
- Put the final answer in attempt_completion (and any response schema fields); do not use progress-message tools to deliver results.
